title: Regsvr32 references a remote scriptlet or DLL
description: Detects regsvr32 command lines that combine the install flag with an HTTP, HTTPS or FTP resource in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process telemetry.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use regsvr32 to retrieve and execute a remote scriptlet or DLL through a trusted Windows binary.
hypothesis.rationale: Regsvr32 with an install flag and a network resource is a recognized signed-binary proxy-execution pattern, but rare administrative or software-installation workflows can produce similar commands.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify regsvr32 processes that combine an install flag with a remote HTTP, HTTPS or FTP resource while leaving local registration and incomplete network patterns unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the referenced network resource and process ancestry, then determine whether regsvr32 launched follow-on code or changed the endpoint.
steps: Review the full regsvr32 command line, remote resource, parent process, user, device and binary path.
Confirm whether an approved installer, software-management product or administrator intentionally used remote registration.
Inspect network connections, downloaded content, child processes and persistence changes; isolate the device when the resource or execution chain is unexplained.
false_positives: Approved installers, software-management products and administrative registration workflows using a remote resource

validation.expected_outcome: Match regsvr32 commands containing both an install flag and a remote protocol; do not match local registration, partial patterns, other processes or incomplete events.
